spans.s:
Vibhaṇḍaka Kāśyapa (‘descendant of kaśyapa’) is the name of a teacher, a pupil of ṛṣyaśṛṅga in the vaṃśa brāhmaṇa.
Foot notes Indische Studīen, 4, 374. Cf. St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v. Vibhāṇḍaka, which is the more correct spelling (Bo7htlingk, Dictionary, s.v.).

Vibhinduka occurs in the pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa as the name of a man or a demon from whom medhātithi drove away the cows. Hopkins is inclined to read Vaibhinduka as a patronymic of medhātithi. Cf. vibhindukīya.
Foot notes xv. 10, 11.
Cf. Sāyaṇa, a.l.
Transactions of the Connecticut Academy of Arts and Sciences, 15, 60, n. 1.

Vibhindukīya is the name of a group of priests whose Sattra is mentioned in the Jaiminīya upaniṣad brāhmaṇa.
Foot notes iii. 233 (Journal of the American Oriental Society, 18, 38).

Vibhītaka and Vibhīdaka, the latter being the old form, denote a large tree, the Terminalia bellerica, the nut of which was used in dicing. The wood was also used for making the sacrificial fire burn.
Foot notes This form is the regular one after the Rigveda.
Rv. vii. 86, 6; x. 34, 1.
Rv., loc. cit. See 2. akṣa.
taittirīya Saṃhitā, ii. 1, 5, 8; 7, 3. Cf. Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, xiii. 8, 1, 16, etc.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 62; Roth, Gurupūjākaumudī, 1-4; Lüders, Das Wūrfelspiel im alten Indien, 17-19.
